title: Marguerite and the Signal
premise: Xanthe Underhill navigates the Marguerite, a freighter carrying illegal memory-backups of people the war has already written off, along a route between colonies that cut contact decades ago. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the whole system, the ship is snared by a dying alien relay that has been holding a peace message hostage since the war's first day — a message that proves the opening strike was an accident on both sides. Delivering it means exposing the backups, including the copy of Xanthe's dead partner, to confiscation; withholding it means the war grinds on. Xanthe chooses to broadcast the message and surrender the backups, and in the final chapter, one backup — the partner's — is quietly returned to them, a small mercy inside a large loss.
about_author: Wren Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years listening to signals no one answered before turning to fiction. They write from a converted observatory on the coast, where they claim the fog improves the endings.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine jump between silent colonies establishes the Marguerite, its skeleton crew, and the sealed hold Xanthe never opens. The beat is weary competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Cargo That Dreams
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We learn the hold holds illegal memory-backups of war casualties, including one of Xanthe's dead partner, Sefa. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Gravity flickers across the system; instruments scream; the Marguerite is dragged off-course mid-jump. The beat is vertigo — the universe hiccuping.

chapters.title: Where the Chart Ends
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The ship drops into uncharted space near a colossal alien relay, dormant for decades, now glowing. Engineer Okafor insists it's a trap; Xanthe feels called. Beat: awe and dread.

chapters.title: The Relay Speaks
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A signal resolves into a message in two languages — human and alien — timestamped the day the war began. Beat: the ground shifting under everything Xanthe believes.

chapters.title: What Sefa Would Say
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, interleaved with a memory of Sefa. The message claims the first strike was a mutual navigation error. Xanthe must decide whether to believe a dead machine. Beat: doubt.

chapters.title: The Hold Question
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor discovers the backups and confronts Xanthe. The relay demands a human carrier to deliver the message through the blockade. Beat: betrayal curdling into uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: Blockade Runners' Gospel
chapters.summary: Crew member Idris's POV. Rumors of a peace faction in the fleet; rumors of bounty on unauthorized signals. The crew votes, badly. Beat: fracturing trust.

chapters.title: Course: Through the War
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They plot a route through contested space to the fleet command at Meridian. Beat: grim commitment, the price already accruing.

chapters.title: First Contact, Again
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. An alien picket ship shadows them; instead of firing, it transmits coordinates — safe passage, in exchange for proof the message is real. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Proof Problem
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Verifying the message requires computing power that would cook the hold's life support. Xanthe must risk the backups to validate the truth. Beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Sefa's Voice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Running the verification, Xanthe accidentally wakes Sefa's backup briefly — ninety seconds of conversation that is both gift and wound. Beat: love that won't stay buried.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris's brother died in the first strike; the message implies it was nobody's fault, which is worse. Beat: grief rejecting absolution.

chapters.title: The Meridian Approach
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The blockade around Meridian is a wall of mines and patrol lanes. They slip in using the relay's gravity trick as cover. Beat: white-knuckle tension.

chapters.title: Admiral Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Fleet command receives them; Voss is pragmatic, exhausted, and convinced the war's logic cannot be undone by one message. Beat: institutional inertia as antagonist.

chapters.title: Evidence and Enemies
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Voss demands the message's origin; revealing the relay also means revealing the backups. Xanthe hesitates. Beat: the secret tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. A crew member — Idris — reports the backups to fleet security, believing it's the only way the message will be heard. Beat: betrayal with good intentions.

chapters.title: Confiscation Order
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Soldiers board the Marguerite and seal the hold. Xanthe watches Sefa's cradle carried away. Beat: loss upon loss, the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Navigator
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Fleet intelligence dissects Xanthe's story; the relay's nine-second flicker is confirmed system-wide — something is waking up out there. Beat: the stakes widening.

chapters.title: The Second Signal
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The relay transmits again: a countdown. If the message isn't broadcast fleet-wide within days, it will go to the aliens directly — and both sides will assume manipulation. Beat: clock starting.

chapters.title: Faction Lines
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The fleet splits: hardliners want the relay destroyed; moderates want the message tested. Idris, guilt-ridden, switches sides. Beat: redemption's first awkward step.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Hardliners bomb the Marguerite's drive to prevent her leaving. Okafor is injured shielding the navigation core. Beat: the ship — and the plan — bleeding.

chapters.title: Repair in the Dark
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe and Idris repair the drive by hand while Voss stalls the hardliners. Beat: reconciliation forged in sparks and silence.

chapters.title: Voss's Gamble
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss decides to let the Marguerite broadcast, betting her career that truth beats doctrine. Beat: an antagonist becoming an ally.

chapters.title: The Hardliner Coup
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Colonel Ashe seizes the broadcast array. The countdown hits its final day. Beat: the door slamming shut.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Again
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Gravity flickers a second time — the relay, dying, is forcing the issue. Every clock in the system resets. Beat: the universe refusing to wait.

chapters.title: Flight to the Array
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The Marguerite runs the blockade inward, using the flicker's gravity wake as a slingshot. Beat: desperate velocity.

chapters.title: Ashe's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Ashe's POV. Ashe offers Xanthe a choice: turn back and the backups go free; continue and he burns them. Xanthe realizes the backups were the leverage all along. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Hold Burns
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Ashe's men vent the hold. Most backups are lost. Xanthe, mid-burn, feels it happen across the ship like a scream cut short. Beat: devastation — the price paid in full.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. One cradle survived, shielded by the navigation core Okafor saved: Sefa's. Okafor hides it and says nothing yet. Beat: a coal kept alive in ash.

chapters.title: Boarding the Array
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe and Idris breach the broadcast station in EVA suits while Ashe's forces close in. Beat: cold, dark, determined.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The message goes out fleet-wide and to the alien fleet simultaneously: the war began as an accident. Beat: catharsis — the truth, finally loud.

chapters.title: Ashe's Last Order
chapters.summary: Ashe's POV. Ordered to fire on the Marguerite, Ashe's own gunners refuse. He stands down, undone not by force but by the message his own crew believes. Beat: the war's logic breaking.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at Meridian
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Weapons go silent across the system, sector by sector. The aliens transmit a single word in human language: 'agreed.' Beat: stunned, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Counted
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Casualty lists, tribunals, the relay going dark forever. Idris visits Xanthe and confesses everything. Beat: accounting, and forgiveness neither asks for nor refuses.

chapters.title: The Empty Hold
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe walks the gutted hold, cataloguing the lost. The Marguerite is offered a new route — between worlds that are speaking again. Beat: mourning with the future faintly visible.

chapters.title: Okafor's Secret
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor reveals Sefa's surviving cradle and the legal fight ahead: one backup, one chance at restoration. Beat: hope offered carefully, like something breakable.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe argues before the reconstruction council that the dead deserve their voices back. Voss testifies for them. Beat: the theme made explicit — what survival owes to memory.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sefa's backup is restored — a copy, not a resurrection, and both of them know it. Their first conversation is about exactly that. Beat: love against duty, resolved honestly.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Underway
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Sefa, shared POV. The Marguerite departs on the reopened route with a small crew and no secrets left. Gravity holds steady. Beat: quiet, earned peace — the signal answered at last.
